q1: SELECT MAX(NUM) AS NUM FROM (SELECT NUM FROM MYNUMBERS GROUP BY NUM HAVING COUNT(NUM) = 1) AS T
q2: SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN TOTAL_COUNT = 1 THEN NUM ELSE NULL END) AS NUM FROM ( SELECT NUM, COUNT(*) AS TOTAL_COUNT FROM MYNUMBERS GROUP BY 1 ) A
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT MAX(NUM) AS NUM FROM (SELECT NUM FROM MYNUMBERS GROUP BY NUM HAVING COUNT(NUM) = 1) AS T
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN TOTAL_COUNT = 1 THEN NUM ELSE NULL END) AS NUM FROM ( SELECT NUM, COUNT(*) AS TOTAL_COUNT FROM MYNUMBERS GROUP BY 1 ) A
explanation: Both queries are designed to find the maximum unique number in the table MYNUMBERS. A number is considered unique if it appears only once in the table. The logic in both queries is equivalent in identifying unique numbers and selecting the maximum among them.
